Model the flow as steady, one-dimensional, isentropic airflow with γ = 1.4 and constant stagnation temperature.
Use the supersonic branch of the area-Mach relation: (A/A*)² = (1/M²)[(2/(γ+1))(1 + ((γ-1)/2)M²)]^((γ+1)/(γ-1)).
Compute A1/A* = 1.6875 and A2/A* = 0.7 × 1.6875 = 1.18125.
Solve the area-Mach relation on the supersonic branch to obtain M2 = 1.5075.
Calculate the velocity ratio using V2/V1 = (M2/M1) × sqrt(T2/T1), where T2/T1 = [1 + ((γ-1)/2)M1²] / [1 + ((γ-1)/2)M2²].
Evaluate V2/V1 = 0.8385.
Report the increase in exit velocity compared to the inlet as V2 − V1 = −16.15% of the inlet velocity, meaning the exit velocity decreases by 16.15%.
